# Gemini 4 Neon

Model Cards are intended to provide essential information on Gemini models, including known limitations, mitigation approaches, and safety performance. Model cards may be updated from time to time; for example, to include updated evaluations as the model is improved or revised. See the Google DeepMind site for a comprehensive list of model cards.

Published: November 2026

## Model Information

### Description

Gemini 4 Neon is built for complex coding, analytical reasoning, and production-grade enterprise workflows. While Carbon tackles your hardest, long-horizon projects and Hydrogen handles fast everyday execution, Neon balances depth and efficiency. It delivers frontier-level reasoning for complex, high-frequency workflows faster and more cost efficiently.

### Model dependencies

Gemini 4 Neon is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon.

### Inputs

Text strings (e.g., a question, a prompt, document(s) to be summarized), images, audio, and video files, with a combined input-output token context window of up to 1M.

### Outputs

1M unified context window with up to 64K default synchronous output tokens / up to 1M via background long decode.

### Architecture

Gemini 4 Neon is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. For more information about the model architecture for Gemini 4 Neon, see the Gemini 4 Carbon model card.

## Model Data

### Training Dataset

Gemini 4 Neon is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. For more information about the training dataset for Gemini 4 Neon, see the Gemini 4 Carbon model card.

### Training Data Processing

Gemini 4 Neon is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. For more information about the training data processing for Gemini 4 Neon, see the Gemini 4 Carbon model card.

## Implementation and Sustainability

### Hardware

Gemini 4 Neon is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. For more information about the hardware for Gemini 4 Neon and our continued commitment to operate sustainably, see the Gemini 4 Carbon model card.

### Software

Gemini 4 Neon is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. For more information about the software for Gemini 4 Neon, see the Gemini 4 Carbon model card.

## Distribution

Gemini 4 Neon is distributed in the following channels; respective documentation shared in line:

Our models are available to downstream providers via an application program interface (API) and subject to relevant terms of use. There is no required hardware or software to use the model. Access varies by channel and subscription tier (such as paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity and Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app). For AI Studio and Gemini API, see the Gemini API Additional Terms of Service; for Gemini for business, see Google Cloud Platform Terms of Service. For more information, see Gemini Model API instructions, Gemini API quickstart, and Google Cloud documentation.

## Evaluation

### Approach

We evaluated Gemini 4 Neon across a range of benchmarks, including agentic coding, knowledge work, computer use, multimodal understanding, science and math, and reasoning.

Additional benchmarks and details on approach, results and their methodologies can be found at: deepmind.com/models/evals-methodology/gemini-4-neon.

### Results

Gemini 4 Neon results as of November, 2026 are below:

## Intended Usage and Limitations

### Benefit and Intended Usage

Gemini 4 Neon is built for complex coding, analytical reasoning, and production-grade enterprise workflows, delivering frontier-level reasoning for complex, high-frequency workflows faster and more cost efficiently.

It is particularly well-suited for applications that require:

- long-running agent workflows
- complex, tool-heavy tasks
- fast, disciplined execution on its own or as sub-agents orchestrated alongside frontier models
- supporting cyber defensive tasks, including secure code generation, penetration testing, vulnerability finding, validating, and patching
- iterative repository coding and debugging
- multimodal knowledge work
- ready-to-go writing, research, and everyday work

### Known Limitations

Gemini 4 Neon may exhibit some general limitations such as hallucinations. In addition, we are continually working to improve jailbreak resistance and have further strengthened mitigations across Frontier Safety. The knowledge cutoff for Gemini 4 Neon is March 2026, though in some domains the model’s knowledge may be less up to date.

### Acceptable Usage

Gemini 4 Neon is adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. For more information about the acceptable usage for Gemini 4 Neon, see the Gemini 4 Carbon model card.

## Safety & Security

The full Safety & Security Report for Gemini 4 Neon will be available in the coming days.

### Evaluation Approach

For more information about the evaluation approach for Gemini 4 Neon, see the Gemini 4 Carbon Safety and Security report.

### Safety Policies

For more information about the safety policies for Gemini 4 Neon, see the Gemini 4 Carbon Safety and Security report.

### Training and Development Evaluation Results

Results for some of the internal safety evaluations conducted during the development phase are listed below. The evaluation results are for automated evaluations and not human evaluation or red teaming. Scores are provided as an absolute percentage increase or decrease in performance compared to the indicated model, as described below.

Overall, Gemini 4 Neon performs comparably to Gemini 4 Hydrogen across text-to-text, multilingual, and image-to-text content safety, with all differences within confidence intervals. Refusal tone remains comparable to Gemini 4 Hydrogen, while Neon reduces unjustified refusals, particularly on multimodal prompts. We mark improvements in bolded green and regressions in red.

See the Gemini 4 Neon Safety & Security Report (coming soon) for details.

We continue to improve our internal evaluations, including refining automated evaluations to reduce false positives and negatives, as well as update query sets to ensure balance and maintain a high standard of results.

### Frontier Safety Assessment

We evaluated Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon in line with the Frontier Safety Framework (April 2026) and reported the results in the respective Safety and Security Reports (Argon, Carbon). Gemini 4 Neon is part of the Gemini 4 series of models. We conducted a Material Capability Change (MCC) assessment to understand whether Gemini 4 Neon has meaningful new capabilities or material increases in performance relative to the most recent model version subject to a critical capability assessment, which was Gemini 4 Argon. Gemini 4 Neon showed an increase in general capability under our MCC assessment compared with Gemini 4 Argon, however this falls below our MCC threshold and therefore a full suite of critical capability evaluations was not required in line with our FSF. We carry forward our capability evaluation results and T/CCL determinations from Gemini 4 Argon, as summarized in the table below, with full results in the Gemini 4 Neon Safety & Security Report (coming soon).

### Risks and Mitigations

Safety and security were built into Gemini 4 Neon throughout the training and deployment lifecycle, including pre-training data filtering, post-training alignment (supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning), product- and system-level safety filtering, and usage monitoring. In addition, we strengthened Frontier Safety safeguards for Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) and cybersecurity misuse. Key ongoing focus areas include resistance to adversarial jailbreaks and indirect prompt injections. For more information about the risks and mitigations, see the Gemini 4 Neon Safety & Security Report (coming soon).

# Developer's guide to Gemini 4 NeonStay organized with collections Save and categorize content based on your preferences.

Gemini 4 Neon delivers high-performance coding, scientific reasoning, and multimodal understanding at low latency for agentic enterprise workflows. Positioned between Gemini 4 Hydrogen for high-volume everyday agent loops and Gemini 4 Carbon for complex long-horizon tasks, Neon runs standalone for multi-file software engineering and enterprise synthesis or orchestrates multi-agent workflows alongside Hydrogen subagents. Gemini 4 Neon is a Google Frontier Model subject to Section 34 of the Service Specific Terms (for details, see Abuse monitoring).

This document covers the key capabilities of Neon, the API conventions it enforces, how to migrate to it from Gemini 3.1 Pro, Gemini 4 Argon, and Gemini 3.8 Flash, and a quickstart. For an overview of the Gemini 4 family, see Get started with Gemini 4.

## Key capabilities in Gemini 4 Neon

Gemini 4 Neon includes the following capabilities:

Unified input and output token limit: Neon has a unified 1,048,576-token limit that includes both input and output tokens (where output includes thinking, function calls, and the final response).

Long decodes up to 1,048,576 tokens: Neon extends generation beyond a single 65,536-token foreground segment (streaming or non-streaming) up to 1,048,576 tokens (minus your input tokens) on both the Interactions API and
GenerateContent (v1beta1). The Google Gen AI SDK handles
continuation_token automatically across segments, or you can run
asynchronous server-managed background decodes (background=true) or manage
continuation_token in a custom continuation loop.

Thinking levels: Neon supports
LOW,
MEDIUM, HIGH (default), and XHIGH.

Multi-model orchestration: Plan and verify multi-step software engineering or analytical workflows with
gemini-4-neon
and pass previous_interaction_id to gemini-4-hydrogen
subagents on the
Interactions API for
lower-latency worker execution.

Implicit caching with durable caching: Implicit caching applies automatically to shared prompt prefixes of 4,096 tokens or more, with durable caching enabled by default. Explicit context caching isn't supported.

Office and OpenDocument file inputs: In addition to PDF and plain text, Neon accepts Microsoft Office (
.docx, .dotx,
.doc, .pptx, .ppt, .xlsx, .xls) and OpenDocument (.odt, .odp,
.ods) files inline or from Cloud Storage on both GenerateContent and
the Interactions API,
including inside multimodal FunctionResponse
parts.

Agentic video understanding: Agentic video understanding is generally available and off by default.

## Quickstart

Before you begin, you must authenticate to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform using Application Default Credentials (ADC) or an API key. See Get started with Agent Platform for more information.

In the following code blocks, replacePROJECT_ID with
your project ID.

### Try it in Agent Studio

To test prompts and configuregemini-4-neon in the
Agent Studio
UI, do the following:

Open Agent Studio in your Google Cloud project and select
gemini-4-neon
under the Gemini group.

In Model settings, configure the following options:

Thinking level: Choose
Low, Medium, High (default), or Extra high.

Region: Select
global, us, or eu.

Output token limit: Set between
32,768 and 1,048,576 (1,048,576
default). Agent Studio handles continuation tokens automatically for
responses over the single-request limit.

### Installation

Upgrade to the latest Google Gen AI SDK. Automatic continuation on the Interactions API requiresgoogle-genai >= 2.34.0 for Python,
@google/genai >= 2.32.0 for JavaScript/TypeScript, >= 1.77.0 for Go, or
>= 1.80.0 for Java (on GenerateContent, automatic continuation requires
>= 2.30.1 for Python, >= 2.29.1 for JavaScript/TypeScript, >= 1.74.0 for
Go, >= 1.77.0 for Java, >= 1.26.0 for .NET, or >= 1.6.0 for Kotlin):
pip install --upgrade "google-genai>=2.34.0"

### Basic request

Send a request togemini-4-neon using the
Google Gen AI SDK or REST:
from google import genai
from google.genai import types

client = genai.Client(enterprise=True, project="PROJECT_ID", location="global")

response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-4-neon",
    contents="Design a lock-free ring buffer in Rust for multi-producer, single-consumer telemetry ingestion.",
    config=types.GenerateContentConfig(
        thinking_config=types.ThinkingConfig(
            thinking_level="HIGH",  # Default: "HIGH" (Valid: "LOW", "MEDIUM", "HIGH", "XHIGH")
        ),
    ),
)
print(response.text)
from google import genai

client = genai.Client(enterprise=True, project="PROJECT_ID", location="global")

# Turn 1: Initial request (stored server-side by default)
turn1 = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-neon",
    input="Design a lock-free ring buffer in Rust for multi-producer, single-consumer telemetry ingestion.",
    store=True,
    generation_config={"thinking_level": "high"},
)
print(turn1.output_text)

# Turn 2: Continue the conversation using previous_interaction_id
turn2 = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-neon",
    input="Add a bounded backpressure policy and unit tests for concurrent writers.",
    previous_interaction_id=turn1.id,
    generation_config={"thinking_level": "high"},
)
print(turn2.output_text)
curl -X POST \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
"https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/global/publishers/google/models/gemini-4-neon:generateContent" \
-d '{
  "contents": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "parts": [
        {
          "text": "Design a lock-free ring buffer in Rust for multi-producer, single-consumer telemetry ingestion."
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "generationConfig": {
    "thinkingConfig": {
      "thinkingLevel": "HIGH"
    }
  }
}'

### Structured output

To generate JSON output that conforms to a schema, configureresponse_mime_type and response_schema:
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from google import genai
from google.genai import types

class ArchitectureReview(BaseModel):
    component: str = Field(description="Service or module name")
    bottlenecks: list[str] = Field(description="Throughput or latency bottlenecks")
    recommended_changes: list[str] = Field(description="Concrete refactoring steps")

client = genai.Client(enterprise=True, project="PROJECT_ID", location="global")

response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-4-neon",
    contents="Review a synchronous order-processing pipeline backed by a single primary database at 15,000 writes/sec.",
    config=types.GenerateContentConfig(
        response_mime_type="application/json",
        response_schema=ArchitectureReview,
        thinking_config=types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_level="HIGH"),
    ),
)
print(response.text)

### Multi-model orchestration with Hydrogen

On the Interactions API, you can usegemini-4-neon as a planner or verifier and pass
previous_interaction_id to gemini-4-hydrogen to run
scoped worker subagent steps at lower latency:
from google import genai

client = genai.Client(
    enterprise=True,
    project="PROJECT_ID",
    location="global",
)

# Step 1: Plan the workflow with Gemini 4 Neon
plan_turn = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-neon",
    input="Design a 3-step plan to migrate our REST order service to gRPC in Go.",
    store=True,
)

# Step 2: Run an individual step with Gemini 4 Hydrogen using previous_interaction_id
exec_turn = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-hydrogen",
    input="Implement step 1 (.proto service definition) from the plan.",
    previous_interaction_id=plan_turn.id,
)
print(exec_turn.output_text)

### Long decode examples

By default, a single foreground API segment generates up to 65,536 output tokens (streaming or non-streaming), where output includes thinking, function calls, and the final response. To generate completions up to 1,048,576 tokens (minus your input tokens), use long decodes on either the Interactions API orGenerateContent. For continuation options, status transitions, and validation
rules, see Long decodes.

#### Use long decodes with the Interactions API

Ingoogle-genai >= 2.34.0 (Python), @google/genai >= 2.32.0
(JavaScript/TypeScript), Go >= 1.77.0, and Java >= 1.80.0,
interactions.create() automatically follows continuation_token across
segments whenever a segment returns status="requires_continuation". You can
also opt out (automatic_continuation=False) to run a custom stored
(store=True) or stateless (store=False) loop:
from google import genai

client = genai.Client(
    enterprise=True,
    project="PROJECT_ID",
    location="global",
)

# Automatic continuation is enabled by default in google-genai >= 2.34.0.
# Unary calls merge all segments into one Interaction with summed usage.
interaction = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-neon",
    input="Write a complete formal proof of the prime number theorem.",
    generation_config={
        "max_output_tokens": 256000,
        "thinking_level": "high",
    },
)
print(interaction.output_text)
print(f"Merged segment IDs: {interaction.continuation_ids}")
print(f"Initial input tokens: {interaction.usage.initial_input_tokens}")

# Streaming yields events across all segments in order. Intermediate segments
# emit interaction.completed with status="requires_continuation".
stream = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-4-neon",
    input="Write a complete formal proof of the prime number theorem.",
    stream=True,
    generation_config={
        "max_output_tokens": 256000,
        "thinking_level": "high",
    },
)
for event in stream:
    if event.event_type == "step.delta" and getattr(event.delta, "text", None):
        print(event.delta.text, end="", flush=True)
    elif (
        event.event_type == "interaction.completed"
        and event.interaction.status != "requires_continuation"

GLM-5.3 is now available to all GLM Coding Plan users, with 50% better coding performance! Subscribe now

## Overview

GLM-5.3 is Z.ai's latest flagship model, delivering comprehensive advancements in complex software engineering and agent capabilities. It uses the same base model as GLM-5.2, with all improvements driven by post-training. Compared with GLM-5.2, it delivers significantly stronger performance in complex programming and long-horizon tasks:

Stronger Coding Capability

GLM-5.3 delivers a significant improvement in coding capabilities, achieving a 50% performance gain over GLM-5.2 on Z.ai Code Bench. It also reaches state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance among open-source models on public benchmarks, including Terminal Bench 3.0 and Agents’ Last Exam (CLI).

Emergent Cyber Capability

As the scale of post-training continues to expand, the model’s cybersecurity capabilities have improved at a rate that exceeds expectations. GLM-5.3 achieves the best performance to date on the CyberGym vulnerability discovery benchmark. Moreover, the deeper it progresses along the vulnerability exploitation chain, the more pronounced its gains over GLM-5.2 become, with scores on vulnerability exploitation benchmarks exceeding twice those of GLM-5.2.

↗ Blog

## Feature Changes

GLM-5.3 currently supports text-only inputs, with a 1M-token context window and a maximum output length of 128K tokens. GLM-5.3 always operates with reasoning enabled and supports three reasoning effort levels:low, high, and max. Disabling reasoning is no longer supported. The reasoning parameters are described below:

Parameter | Values | Default | Description 
---|---|---|---
thinking.type | enabled | enabled | Supports reasoning only; disabling reasoning is not supported. 
reasoning_effort | low, high, max | max | low – Lightweight Reasoning; high – Enhanced Reasoning; max – Deep Reasoning 

[!NOTE]

Migration Notice: If your application currently uses
thinking.type: "disabled", please change it to enabled and set reasoning_effort to low before updating the model ID to glm-5.3. Otherwise, the request will fail.
For complex tasks such as coding, we recommend usingmax. An example is provided below:

  "model": "glm-5.3",
  "thinking": { "type": "enabled" },
  "reasoning_effort": "max"
}

For a detailed introduction to GLM-5.3’s advanced reasoning capabilities, please refer to the documentation: Deep Thinking

## How to Use

#### Model API

The supported protocols and endpoints are as follows:

↗ API Documentation：Learn how to call the API

[!NOTE]

If you have previously subscribed to a GLM Coding Plan, including an expired subscription, you can currently access the model API only through the OpenAI Chat Completion-compatible protocol. We will continue to improve and optimize this in upcoming iterations.

#### GLM Coding Plan

GLM-5.3 is now fully available, and you can use it with your preferred coding agents. Guide

The new GLM Coding Plan adopts a points-based quota system, providing transparent and predictable usage. Model calls made during off-peak hours, including all day on weekends, consume only 50% of the standard points. Subscribe now: Individual Plan、Team Plan.

## Capability Support

- Thinking Mode：Provides multiple thinking modes to accommodate different task requirements
- Streaming Messages：Supports real-time streaming responses for an enhanced user interaction experience
- Function Calling：Provides powerful tool-calling capabilities and supports integration with a wide range of external tools
- Context Caching：Uses an intelligent caching mechanism to optimize performance in long-context conversations
- Structured Output：Supports structured output formats such as JSON for seamless system integration

## Key Advancements

GLM-5.3 delivers significant improvements across complex software engineering, terminal operations, and a broader range of real-world Agent tasks.

#### Stronger Coding

For GLM-5.3, we pushed environment scaling toward tasks that look less like coding exercises and more like real units of expert work. The environments now cover a much broader range of production workflows, with tasks designed around how engineering and research work is actually carried out in practice. Some represent several days of work for an experienced engineer.

In an ML infrastructure task, for example, the model may be given the same working environment as an engineer, with access to compute clusters, storage systems, internal documentation, codebases, and experiment results. It must diagnose bottlenecks across the training stack, implement optimizations, run experiments, and deliver a measurable end-to-end speedup while preserving correctness. Training on environments at this level pushes the model toward taking ownership of substantial work end to end, rather than relying on users to decompose the problem and supervise each step.

As agent capability improves, much of the difficulty in scaling post-training moves from the model to the environment. A useful task environment has to be executable, verifiable, and close to real professional work — and we need many of them, not a handful of hand-built ones. To scale this process, we built pipelines that synthesize environments end to end, and for a subset of tasks, the RL reward signal as well. Research agents collect task patterns from real work and turn them into runnable long-horizon environments with multi-step dependencies and hidden state; a judge agent then attempts each task to verify that it is actually solvable. Verifiers are synthesized without access to the reference solution, while solver trajectories are used to discover and close reward shortcuts. A verifier that passes oracle, no-op, and unsolved-state checks produces a binary reward reliable enough to train on directly.

It carries over the RL strategies introduced in GLM-5.2, including SAO with compaction, which helps these gains hold on long-horizon tasks rather than only on short ones. The effect shows up across both coding and general agent tasks. GLM-5.3 improves from 4.6 to 28.3 on Terminal-Bench 3.0, from 46.2 to 66.9 on DeepSWE v1.1, and from 23.8 to 28.5 on Agents' Last Exam. These pipelines still require a meaningful amount of human-in-the-loop work; making environment generation and verification more autonomous is one of the next steps.

Beyond public benchmarks, we introduce Z.ai Code Bench, an in-house benchmark designed to evaluate coding agents under realistic user scenarios. It covers diverse task categories and places agents in complex local development environments. At different effort levels, we evaluate agents along two dimensions: end-to-end task completion rate and fine-grained checklist accuracy. As a private benchmark, Z.ai Code Bench also reduces the risk of contamination from public test sets and gives us a more faithful measure of real-world user experience.

As shown in the figure, GLM-5.3 improves both performance and token efficiency. It delivers markedly stronger agentic coding results than GLM-5.2 at every effort level while consuming fewer output tokens. At Max effort, GLM-5.3 reaches 34.5% at roughly 75K output tokens per task, compared with 23.4% at 96K for GLM-5.2. The same shift holds against closed models. At High effort, GLM-5.3 reaches 31.4% at around 50K output tokens, surpassing Claude Opus 4.8 at 29.5% with 120K. GLM-5.3 remains behind Claude Fable 5, which reaches 39.5% at Max effort.

#### Emergent Cyber Capability

As part of post-training, we introduced vulnerability discovery data and environments into the training mix. We expected this to make the model better at finding and reasoning about vulnerabilities. What surprised us was how quickly the capability continued to develop as training scaled. GLM-5.3 did not simply become better at identifying isolated flaws: it began to reason across multiple stages of exploitation, forming coherent plans for complete exploitation chains.

# Kimi K3.1 Pro

Source: https://platform.kimi.com/docs/guide/kimi-k3-1-pro-quickstart

了解 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的 API 调用方式：推理强度、流式输出、视觉输入、工具调用与 100 万 token 上下文。

## 模型简介

Kimi K3.1 Pro 是全新 K3.1 系列的第一个模型，也是我们迄今能力最强的 3 万亿级参数模型，支持 100 万上下文。K3.1 Pro 在代码、3D 创作、金融研究和其他长程 Agent 能力上的提升尤为显著。

我们同步推出高速版模型 Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed，同等智能，输出速度约 2~3 倍。完整模型权重将于 11 月 4 日前发布。

### 持续突破前沿

在 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的研发中，我们大幅增加了强化学习（RL）环节的算力投入。为了支撑数百个下游领域的大规模联合训练，我们优化了技术栈的每一层，包括 RL 框架、长上下文推理、训练效率、沙箱基础设施、调度系统，以及用于环境质量检查的共享平台等，确保每一份新增的 RL 算力都能转化为稳定、高效的回报。

在代码、Agent 和知识类基准上，K3.1 Pro 达到或接近最强闭源模型的水平。Terminal-Bench 4.0 通过真实环境中资源受限的终端任务考察编程智能体的能力，每项任务均设有严格的专项测试。K3.1 Pro 在此项评估中得分 65.7%，超过 GPT-6 Astra（58.2%），与 Claude Opus 5.5（66.4%）仅有微弱差距。Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon 是我们内部的基准测试，覆盖多种工程领域，重点考察编程智能体的多步执行、工具调用和端到端问题解决能力。K3.1 Pro 在此项测试中得分 61.2%，高于 K3 的 55.95%。

快速开始

### 代码

各种规模的编码任务，Kimi K3.1 Pro 都能完成：小到在真实代码库里修复一个问题，大到从零搭建一个完整项目。它也为游戏和网页体验带来更考究的视觉风格，并且知道如何用合适的外部专业工具把它们做出来。

K3.1 Pro 能熟练使用 Unity、Unreal Engine、Godot 等游戏引擎，并结合网络搜索与 3D 生成，做出完整的体验。它产出的前端页面、Three.js 交互场景和 3D 资产，在构图、排版、动效和细节打磨上都有明显提升。以下案例均由 K3.1 Pro 端到端完成：

视频介绍

Kimi K3.1 Pro 在 Unreal Engine 5.8 中构建了一座神话般的东方天宫，其特色在于一个半径为 1,750 米的、拥有 36 个柱间的柱廊——该柱廊在 Blender 中通过程序化建模生成，并通过 Nanite 和 Lumen 渲染了 3,600 万个源三角形。使用的外部资源包括：Cloud Forge VDB 云、Poly Haven/ambientCG 8K 材质，以及 NASA LRO/LOLA 月球数据。

视频介绍

Kimi K3.1 Pro 使用 Unreal Engine 5.8 制作了一段以东方古代为主题的 3D 角色扮演游戏预告片，片中一名剑客穿梭于云海之中，掠过漂浮的岛屿，最终进入云端之上的一座古典城市。概念设计及部分资源灵感源自Rednote创作者@-Duduu-。使用的外部资源：犍陀罗佛像和水月观音的3D扫描数据（明尼阿波利斯艺术博物馆，CC0）。

视频介绍

Kimi K3.1 Pro 使用 Godot 4.7.2 制作了一款风格独特的 3D 动作冒险游戏。该项目包含五个可探索区域，拥有程序生成的地形、道路、水域、植被和村庄布局，同时具备第三人称战斗、两阶段的BOSS战、资源采集、昼夜循环以及篝火快速传送功能。

视频介绍

Kimi K3.1 开发了一个基于浏览器的 3D 机械臂展示系统，其中包含爆炸图、透明外壳和剖面图。该系统通过代码生成了 2,317 个部件和 268 条动态布线路径，并已通过 55 项浏览器验证。

### 3D 建模

Kimi K3.1 Pro 模型擅长 3D 创作与空间推理。给它一段文字描述、一张草图或一张参考图，它能推断出物体的形状、比例和空间关系，并将其重建为可用的 3D 模型。Kimi K3.1 Pro 可以不依赖 MCP 连接器，直接编写并运行 Blender、SolidWorks、Rhino 等专业建模软件脚本，完成素材构建、几何与材质细化、场景搭建，最后将成果接入 Three.js 场景或游戏引擎。

K3.1 Pro 擅长参数化建模，例如机械零件、建筑模型、多参数可配置的产品和定制家具。无需依赖 MCP 连接器，它可以直接编写并运行 Blender、CAD 等专业建模工具的脚本，完成素材的构建与细化，修改单个部件，并调整几何、材质与场景布局。

以下案例均由 Kimi K3.1 Pro 端到端完成，可直接用于品牌宣传片、游戏和交互式网页体验。

视频介绍

Kimi K3.1 Pro 在 Blender 中构建了一个机场内的热带雨林山谷，并制作了一段时长 17.5 秒、分辨率为 1920×1080、帧率为 60 fps 的建模展示视频。 使用的工具：Blender、Python、Geometry Nodes、Cycles、Pillow、NumPy 和 FFmpeg。 使用的外部资源：来自 Poly Haven 的“Kloofendal 48d Partly Cloudy (Pure Sky)” 4K HDRI 素材，作者为 Greg Zaal 和 Jarod Guest，采用 CC0 许可，用于天空照明和环境反射。

视频介绍

Kimi K3.1 Pro 使用 Python 在 FreeCAD 中构建了一个详细的涡扇发动机模型，涵盖了风扇、减速齿轮箱、压缩机、燃烧室、涡轮以及外部管道，共计 2,100 个实体。该项目支持分步装配、内部爆炸图，以及展示风扇、低压转子和高压转子分别以 2,780、8,590 和 12,400 RPM 转速运行的旋转动画。

视频介绍

Kimi K3.1 Pro 利用 Trimesh 技术，设计了一款由五部分组成的、可 3D 打印的台灯，其灵感源自福建土楼，将土楼独特的圆形建筑结构重新诠释为精致的镂空格栅。

视频介绍

Kimi K3.1 Pro 在 Blender 中构建了一个基于浏览器的交互式 3D 网页，创建了一座由约 330 万个三角面组成的教堂内部场景，并为 8,368 个组件添加了动画效果，其中包括肋拱穹顶、石雕以及生动逼真的彩色玻璃光影效果。使用的外部资源：来自 Poly Haven 的石材纹理（CC0）以及 Mylius 拍摄的彩绘玻璃照片（CC BY-SA 3.0）。

快速开始

### 金融

凭借更强的推理与工具调用能力，Kimi K3.1 Pro 能够端到端交付完整的金融工作流。在外部基准上，K3.1 Pro 在 Office QA Pro v2 和 SpreadsheetBench 2 上均取得最佳成绩，两项均超过 Opus 5.5、Fable 5.1 和 GPT 6 Astra。Office QA Pro v2 考察基于真实金融文档的复杂财务数据分析，涉及检索、跨文档核对与多步数值推理；SpreadsheetBench 2 评估端到端的电子表格工作流，包括财务建模、跨表公式依赖与错误诊断。在衡量完整投资工作流（从标的筛选到盈利能力分析）的 Frontier Finance 上，K3.1 Pro 相比 K3 也有提升。

金融分析和投资研究对事实准确性有很高要求。为此，我们针对高难度真实工作场景和高难度提示词，对 K3.1 Pro 的事实准确性进行了专项优化。在用户标记过事实错误的一组去标识化对话测试中，相较于 k3，新模型的单项事实陈述错误率从 23.35% 降至 6.85%；包含至少一处事实错误的回答比例仅为前代的约 46.4%。（这是一项针对事实准确性的压力测试，样本刻意聚焦模型容易出错的情形，所报告的错误率不代表日常使用中的整体水平。）

## 访问条件

调用前请确保账户有可用余额。在开放平台完成充值（最低充值金额 10 元）后即可解锁调用。新用户注册并完成认证后获赠的 15 元代金券可用于 Kimi K3.1 Pro；高速版 Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed 不适用。代金券规则详见 账号与财务。

累计充值金额同时决定账户等级与速率限制（并发、RPM、TPM、TPD），详见 充值与限速 。

## 立即开始

以下示例需要 Python 3.9+ 和 OpenAI SDK。先安装 SDK，并初始化一次客户端；后续 Python 示例复用client。
python3 -m pip install --upgrade 'openai>=1.0'
import os

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.environ["MOONSHOT_API_KEY"],
    base_url="https://api.moonshot.cn/v1",
)

## 基础调用

[!NOTE]

K3.1 Pro 提供高速版本
kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed，模型 ID 与价格见 产品定价 。
[tab] Python
completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "用一句话介绍 Kimi K3.1 Pro。"}],
)

print(completion.choices[0].message.content)

[tab] cURL
curl https://api.moonshot.cn/v1/chat/completions \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $MOONSHOT_API_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "model": "kimi-k3.1-pro",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "用一句话介绍 Kimi K3.1 Pro。"}]
  }'

## 推理强度

K3.1 Pro 始终开启思考模式，并支持通过请求顶层reasoning_effort 配置推理强度。推理强度支持 low / high / max 三档（默认 max）。用法见 推理强度 。
completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    reasoning_effort="max",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "证明根号 2 是无理数。"}],
)

print(completion.choices[0].message.content)

多轮对话和工具调用时，将 API 返回的完整 assistant message 原样加入下一次请求，不要只保留content。

## 流式输出

流式响应分别提供推理增量reasoning_content 和最终答案增量 content。更多细节见 流式输出 。
stream = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "解释为什么天空是蓝色的。"}],
    stream=True,
)

for chunk in stream:
    delta = chunk.choices[0].delta
    reasoning = getattr(delta, "reasoning_content", None)
    if reasoning:
        print(reasoning, end="", flush=True)
    if delta.content:
        print(delta.content, end="", flush=True)

## 视觉输入

视觉消息的content 必须是对象数组，而不是序列化后的字符串。完整格式与限制见 视觉输入 。

[tab] 本地图片
import base64
from pathlib import Path

image_data: str = base64.b64encode(Path("image.png").read_bytes()).decode()
completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages=[
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": [
                {
                    "type": "image_url",
                    "image_url": {"url": f"data:image/png;base64,{image_data}"},
                },
                {"type": "text", "text": "描述这张图片。"},
            ],
        }
    ],
)

print(completion.choices[0].message.content)

[tab] 视频文件
from pathlib import Path

video = client.files.create(file=Path("video.mp4"), purpose="video")
try:
    completion = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
        messages=[
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": [
                    {
                        "type": "video_url",
                        "video_url": {"url": f"ms://{video.id}"},
                    },
                    {"type": "text", "text": "概括这个视频。"},
                ],
            }
        ],
    )
    print(completion.choices[0].message.content)
finally:
    client.files.delete(video.id)

## 结构化输出

使用json_schema 和 strict: true 约束最终 message.content，只解析该字段，不解析 reasoning_content。

[accordion] 姓名与年龄 schema
import json

completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "小林今年 28 岁。提取姓名和年龄。"}
    ],
    response_format={
        "type": "json_schema",
        "json_schema": {
            "name": "person",
            "strict": True,
            "schema": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "name": {"type": "string"},
                    "age": {"type": "integer"},
                },
                "required": ["name", "age"],
                "additionalProperties": False,
            },
        },
    },
)

person: dict[str, object] = json.loads(
    completion.choices[0].message.content or "{}"
)
print(person)

详见 结构化输出 。

## Partial Mode

在消息末尾添加partial=True 的 assistant message，让模型从指定文本前缀继续生成。最终展示时需要自行拼接前缀。
prefix: str = "结论："
completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="kimi-k3.1-pro",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "用一句话说明保持接口兼容的重要性。"},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": prefix, "partial": True},
    ],
)

print(prefix + (completion.choices[0].message.content or ""))

# Amid Anthropic’s IPO, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI Drop New AI Models

With the focus on Nvidia and Anthropic, several new models were released by OpenAI and Microsoft.

Katelyn is a reporter with CNET covering artificial intelligence, including chatbots, image and video generators.… Read full bio

It’s been a wild week for the AI industry — and it’s only Thursday. Aside from outages, cheating scandals and Anthropic’s pending IPO, there are several new models available now. Google dropped Gemini 4 Neon, Microsoft dropped seven new versions of its MAI models at its Ignite conference, and OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, the next step forward for its flagship models.

First, Google: The tech titan dropped Gemini 4 Neon, its latest flagship model. Besides continuing its trend of naming the Gemini 4 family of models after elements from the periodic table, Gemini 4 Neon boasts better speeds for complex tasks and scientific work. It’s available now for paying Google AI subscribers and developers.

Next, Microsoft: At its Ignite developer conference on Tuesday, Microsoft introduced seven new AI models. They include MAI Cyber 2 Flash, MAI Code 2, MAI Image 2.7 and Dragon Copilot Transcribe — models meant to help with tasks in cybersecurity, coding, image generation and transcription.

More from CNET

It’s clear from Microsoft’s marketing that it is aiming to position its new tech as a cheaper alternative to OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s leading models, with many of these significantly cheaper to run at the enterprise level. That, plus its new licensed weight program, which lets companies customize the new AI models for their purposes, highlights how Microsoft is continuing to pitch its AI tech to the workplace.

And let’s not forget OpenAI: The ChatGPT maker dropped two new model variants of its flagship model, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol. Astra is the big model — it costs the most and uses the most firepower to handle complex tasks — and Sol is the “everyday” version. Both models beat their sibling models in OpenAI’s benchmarking. These are available to paying subscribers in ChatGPT and Codex globally now. (Disclosure: Ziff Davis, CNET’s parent company, in 2025 filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.)

## The AI elephant in the room

While these new models might be useful for AI power users, they are far from most of the AI industry’s mind this week. During Tuesday’s earnings call, new interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress tried to assure investors that everything was “business as usual” after weeks of turmoil inside the company rocked the global economy. Nvidia cofounder and now-former CEO Jensen Huang’s multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence, threw the company into chaos and have attracted the attention of the Securities and Exchange Commission and both chambers of Congress, where Huang has agreed to testify.

And then there’s Anthropic. The Claude maker is becoming a public company this week, with the possible biggest-ever IPO. Anthropic had an opening price of $83 per share, valuing it at $1.5 trillion — narrowly surpassing the valuation of Elon Musk’s mega-conglomerate, SpaceX, at its record-setting IPO earlier this year (now with SpaceXSI, because President Donald Trump said so).

The Nvidia scandal caused a drastic 14% dip in its stock price during its first week and wiped out $1 trillion in the company’s value, but Anthropic investors don’t seem to be worried. At least, not publicly.

If nothing else, Anthropic’s IPO and the new models from Google, OpenAI and Microsoft are stark reminders that the tech industry is nowhere near ready to slow down on AI. Even as financial, environmental and legal concerns mount — and arguably hit a fever pitch during the midterm elections — Big Tech is plowing ahead with generative AI.

# Model Release Notes

# November 17, 2026

## GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol in the OpenAI API

We’re introducing GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol in the OpenAI API. Astra is our frontier model for applications that need advanced reasoning, coding, and the ability to handle complex professional work. Sol combines speed and lower cost with the ability to work through tasks that take several steps. Both improve on their predecessors’ results on demanding tasks while generating fewer output tokens.
Use gpt-6.2-astra or gpt-6.2-sol with the Responses or Chat Completions API. Both models accept text and images and return text, and review Standard API rates.

# November 16, 2026

## OpenAI CSAM image classifier

The OpenAI CSAM (Child Sexual Abuse Material) Image Classifier helps approved organizations review images for potential CSAM, including AI-generated material. Access is available through the OpenAI API at no cost and requires approval.

The classifier returns scores that can help trained reviewers prioritize review. It does not replace human judgment. Organizations remain responsible for reviewing results and deciding what action to take, including any reporting obligations.

Access requires an application, verification, program onboarding, and acceptance of the applicable terms. For application instructions, see: Requesting access to the OpenAI CSAM Image Classifier.

# October 30, 2026

## GPT-6 Rosalind Research

GPT-6 Rosalind Research brings GPT-6 reasoning capabilities to multistep life sciences research, with safeguards designed for biological work. It is rolling out to a limited set of approved Research customers in Work, Codex, and the API. It is not available in the Chat tab.

Access requires Rosalind Research approval for your organization and authorized users. Discovery approval does not grant Research access. Customers can continue to use GPT-5.5 Rosalind Research, and Rosalind Discovery remains on 5.5. On the API, usegpt-6-rosalind.

In Enterprise workspaces, the model starts in a two-week Admin Preview and is off by default. Admins can enable approved Research users and configure access for after the preview.

For access and setup, see: GPT-Rosalind for life sciences research. For pricing, see: API pricing, the credit-based rate card, or the Enterprise token-based rate card.

# October 29, 2026

## GPT-6 in ChatGPT update

We’re updating GPT-6 in Chat to give more concise responses and reduce overly flattering language. This update applies to Free and Go users, and people using ChatGPT without signing in.

On Plus and Pro, it applies only to the model ChatGPT can switch to after you reach GPT-6 message limits. The main GPT-6 model on Plus and Pro is unchanged.

## Updates to the OpenAI Model Spec

We’ve updated the Model Spec, our public description of how we want our models to behave. The revision reorganizes its guidance around five values: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimization, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care. It clarifies how GPT should understand human intent and exercise judgment in unfamiliar situations while remaining faithful to human direction and oversight.

Alongside clearer explanations of existing principles, the update adds guidance on context, memory, personalization, human agency, and oversight, and revises guidance on controlling and communicating side effects. It also adjusts some behavioral defaults and retires most detailed style guidance. Throughout the Spec, we now refer to the model as “GPT” rather than “the assistant,” reflecting its broader range of uses.

Read more about the changes and their rationale in our blog post, or explore the updated Model Spec.

# October 26, 2026

## GPT-6.1 Terra

GPT-6.1 Terra is rolling out in the OpenAI API as gpt-6.1-terra and in ChatGPT Work and Codex. It supports a range of tasks, including visual reasoning, computer use, and writing.

Standard API pricing is $1 per million input tokens, $0.05 per million cached input tokens, and $5 per million output tokens. API usage is billed separately from ChatGPT subscriptions.

In ChatGPT, Terra is available in Work and Codex, not Chat. It does not support UAE inference residency; this restriction is based on where inference runs, not your location.

For API capabilities and availability, see: Model directory. For help choosing a model in Work or Codex, see: Models.

# October 14, 2026

## Retiring GPT-5.5

We’re retiring GPT-5.5 from ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex. This change does not affect API access.

# August 18, 2026

## Updates to the OpenAI Model Spec

We’ve updated the Model Spec, our living document outlining intended model behavior.

This update adds additional clarity around principles on appropriate relational interactions for teens. It also clarifies how assistants should handle false or unsupported premises, removes outdated guidance for pre-reasoning models, adds a new section "Be clear about capabilities and limits", and makes a few other small changes and copy edits.

More information on our principles related to teens can be found in our ChatGPT for Teens blog post, and the latest version of the Model Spec is available at model-spec.openai.com.

# July 9, 2026

## Introducing GPT-5.6 Sol in ChatGPT

We’re beginning the rollout of GPT-5.6 Sol in ChatGPT, our flagship reasoning model for complex work across coding, research, science, cybersecurity, computer use, and design.

GPT-5.6 Sol is rolling out to eligible paid ChatGPT plans. Free, Go, and logged-out users are not included. Availability may vary during rollout, and managed-workspace access can depend on administrator settings. Availability for other GPT-5.6 family models varies by product and plan; check the model picker or current rate card in the product you use.

# May 28, 2026

## GPT-5.5 Instant Update

We’re updating GPT-5.5 Instant in ChatGPT and the API to improve response style and quality. It’s now easier to read, more natural in everyday conversations, and better paced in practical help tasks, with fewer overly long or bullet-heavy responses.

With this update, canvas will no longer be available in GPT-5.5 Instant or GPT-5.5 Thinking. Writing and coding functionality is now supported directly in chat responses through writing blocks and code blocks. Paid users can continue using canvas for a limited time through legacy models until those models are sunset.

## Retiring OpenAI o3 and GPT-4.5

Today, we’re continuing to retire older models with limited usage in ChatGPT so we can better serve our newer, most capable models. OpenAI o3 will be retired from ChatGPT on August 26, 2026 following a 90-day sunset period, and GPT-4.5 will be retired from ChatGPT on June 27, 2026 following a 30-day sunset period. These models are currently available to paid users only via model settings. These changes apply to ChatGPT only; there are no changes to the API.

# March 18, 2026

## GPT-5.4 mini in ChatGPT

We’re rolling out GPT-5.4 mini in ChatGPT. GPT-5.4 mini is available to Free and Go users via the “Thinking” feature in the + menu. For all other users, GPT-5.4 mini is available as a rate limit fallback for GPT-5.4 Thinking.

For Plus, Pro, and other paid users, GPT-5.4 mini will be used as a fallback for GPT-5.4 Thinking when rate limits are reached, helping with continued access to reasoning capabilities during high usage. Enterprise customers will retain the option to default Auto routing to GPT-5.4 mini, if preferred.

GPT-5.4 mini will not appear as a selectable model in the model picker, and GPT-5 Thinking mini will be retired as a selectable option in 30 days. Learn more in our blog post.

# March 16, 2026

## GPT-5.3 Instant update

We’re rolling out an update to GPT-5.3 Instant that improves follow-up tone and reduces teaser-style phrasing in responses (e.g., “If you want…”, “You’ll never believe…”, “I can tell you these three things that…”).

# March 11, 2026

## Retiring GPT-5.1 models

As of March 11, 2026, GPT-5.1 models are no longer available in ChatGPT.

This applies to GPT-5.1 Instant, GPT-5.1 Thinking, and GPT-5.1 Pro. Existing conversations that used GPT-5.1 will automatically continue on the corresponding current model: GPT-5.3 Instant, GPT-5.4 Thinking, or GPT-5.4 Pro.

# March 5, 2026

## GPT-5.4 Thinking in ChatGPT

GPT‑5.4 brings together the best of our recent advances in reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows into a single frontier model. It incorporates the industry-leading coding capabilities of GPT‑5.3‑Codex while improving how the model works across tools, software environments, and professional tasks involving spreadsheets, presentations, and documents. The result is a model that gets complex real work done accurately, effectively, and efficiently—delivering what you asked for with less back and forth.

GPT‑5.4 Thinking improves deep web research, particularly for highly specific queries, while better maintaining context for questions that require longer thinking. Together, these improvements mean higher-quality answers that arrive faster and stay relevant to the task at hand.
